# NormalizedDescriptors

A C++ port of the `RDKit2DHistogramNormalized` descriptors from
[descriptastorus](https://github.com/bp-kelley/descriptastorus).

Each descriptor value is mapped to the fraction of a reference population with
the same or a smaller value, using a cumulative histogram of that population:
the value takes the cumulative fraction of the first bin whose left edge is
`>=` the value, or `1.0` past the last edge. There is no interpolation and no
clipping, so lookups match descriptastorus' `bins[bisect(bins, (v,))][1]`
exactly.

Descriptors without a table, descriptors that cannot be computed, and NaN
values normalize to `0.0`, as in descriptastorus.

The extension is built when `RDK_BUILD_NORMALIZED_DESCRIPTORS` is `ON` (the
default).

## Tables

`data/normalized_descriptor_histograms.txt` holds one cumulative histogram per
descriptor. The first 201 come unchanged from descriptastorus' `hists.py`; the
rest are binned from `chembl_100k.smi` the same way. It is generated by
`tools/fit_normalized_descriptors.py`; see `tools/README.md` for the format and
for adding descriptors. The histograms were made with an older RDKit and may
need to be rebuilt with a current one.

## Usage

`calcNormalizedDescriptors` computes the 217 descriptors in
`rdkit.Chem.Descriptors._descList` (same names, same order, given by
`getNormalizedDescriptorNames`) and normalizes them. As in descriptastorus, a
descriptor that cannot be computed or has no table gives `0.0`.

C++:

```c++
#include <GraphMol/NormalizedDescriptors/NormalizedDescriptors.h>

using namespace RDKit::NormalizedDescriptors;
const auto &names = getNormalizedDescriptorNames();
std::vector<double> vals = calcNormalizedDescriptors(mol);  // default tables
std::vector<double> raw = calcDescriptorValues(mol);         // unnormalized
double v = getDefaultTables().normalize("MolLogP", 2.5);

// lookups by index skip the name lookup; normalizeDescriptors() uses table
// indices cached when the tables are loaded
const auto &tables = getDefaultTables();
int idx = tables.getTableIndex("MolLogP");
double v2 = tables.normalize(idx, 2.5);
std::vector<double> normalized = tables.normalizeDescriptors(raw);
```

Python:

```python
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import rdNormalizedDescriptors as rdnd
names = rdnd.GetNormalizedDescriptorNames()
vals = rdnd.CalcNormalizedDescriptors(Chem.MolFromSmiles('c1ccccc1O'))
rdnd.NormalizeDescriptor('MolLogP', 2.5)
```

`test_data/reference_descriptors.tsv` holds `rdkit.Chem.Descriptors` values
for a few molecules (from `test_data/make_reference.py`); the tests check the
C++ calculation against it.
